key_reasoning.reason: New headless-driver module drives the codemie CLI over a live PTY byte stream (base64-decoded and fed into a headless xterm.js Terminal), re-parsing the screen on every chunk with no exact existing precedent in the codebase; involves a single-flight lock, a per-run prompt-signature dedup guard, an in-flight guard against concurrent redraws during model-list pagination, and an idle-timer heuristic (IDLE_MS/YN_HINT) to disambiguate 'CLI still working' from 'unclassified stalled prompt' -- several defect-fix comments (CR-001..CR-005) in setup-driver.js confirm these edge cases surfaced only during implementation.

New setup-driver.js module coordinates 3 components across the frontend: itself (prompt state machine), setup-parse.js's detectPrompt/isQ (reused, minor edits), and terminal.js's suspendPtyInput/resumePtyInput -- a change to a core shared utility (terminal.js) consumed by other PTY-driven flows (wizard steps, home-page proxy/analytics actions), not just this feature.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from L to XL: real-time/streaming PTY byte-stream handling (onData callback processing live terminal redraws chunk-by-chunk)

Component Scope bumped from M to L: touches terminal.js, a core shared utility used by other PTY-driven flows beyond this feature (suspendPtyInput/resumePtyInput now gate all keystroke forwarding during a setup run)
